answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by issuing reputation only against a bonded stake plus proof that one human seed funded the node once. Cloning a wallet copies nothing of value, while genuine collateral is paid per identity and slashed on coupled misbehaviour. Identity then spreads like a slow ocean current, not a burst of bots. A fresh Sybil cluster sits like a raw opal: unwitnessed and unable to vouch for peers. Trust builds along a spiral of attested trades, each peer check costing the attacker more than the vote it buys.
